title: MolyJam 2013

contributors.contribution: Created the character artwork and still-image cutscene artwork.

description: For the 48-hour MolyJam 2013, I built a complete first-person voxel adventure game on my Java/LWJGL ShaderBox engine. The game combined five Peter Molydeux-inspired prompts into a single progression-driven world with sword combat, exploration, collectibles, animated environments, scripted objectives, a giant boss encounter, and a princess rescue. I hand-built the entire voxel level in Qubicle, created the textures, and completed and submitted the game within the jam deadline.

sections.title: 48-Hour Solo Development
paragraphs: I participated remotely from home through the worldwide MolyJam website, where developers registered, posted progress during the weekend, and submitted completed games for community rating.
I completed the game within the 48-hour deadline as the sole developer.

sections.title: Built on ShaderBox
paragraphs: The game was built directly on my ShaderBox Java/LWJGL 3D engine rather than a commercial game engine.
ShaderBox provided the underlying 3D rendering, world, camera, model, shader, and voxel systems used by the game.

sections.title: Hand-Built Voxel World
paragraphs: I hand-authored the complete game world in Qubicle rather than generating the terrain procedurally.
The level was designed as a connected adventure space with exterior terrain, water, temples, a mountain interior, lava areas, a castle, and a summit encounter.

sections.title: Adventure Progression
paragraphs: The player begins outside the mountain and must explore the world to discover how to gain access to the interior.
A tap/lever opens the mouth of a giant goblin-head mountain, allowing the player to enter and continue through lava areas, a temple, and a castle before climbing toward the summit.

sections.title: Final Rescue
paragraphs: At the top of the mountain, a giant guards the red-haired princess.
The giant cannot be defeated directly; the player must avoid its crushing attacks long enough to reach and rescue the princess.

sections.title: First-Person Combat
paragraphs: The game uses a first-person viewpoint and gives the player a sword for close-range combat.
Several troll enemy variants populate the level and can be defeated with the sword, while the giant boss functions as an environmental threat rather than a conventional killable enemy.

sections.title: Exploration & Optional Areas
paragraphs: The world includes optional and side areas beyond the main rescue path.
items: A pirate ship located in the water
A small boat that chases the player around a river
Cannon fire from the pursuing boat
A guarded temple containing the golden acorn

sections.title: Five Molydeux Prompts
paragraphs: The game intentionally combined five separate Molydeux-style prompts into one playable adventure rather than treating them as unrelated jokes.

sections.title: Win a Ginger-Haired Person
paragraphs: The prompt about going into battle and winning a ginger-haired person became the main objective: surviving the journey and rescuing the red-haired princess.

sections.title: What Do the Taps Mean?
paragraphs: The tap became a functional progression device.
Activating it opens the giant goblin-head mountain and gives the player access to the interior portion of the level.

sections.title: The Most Interesting Thing in the World
paragraphs: Pulling the appropriate trigger activates the joke associated with the prompt 'see the most interesting thing in the world': an image of Peter Molydeux begins following the player around the game world.

sections.title: Golden Acorn
paragraphs: The golden acorn is hidden in a guarded temple.
After surviving the surrounding traps, the player can collect it and receives a message acknowledging that they survived and may keep the acorn.

sections.title: Collect a Million Gold Coins
paragraphs: Coins are distributed throughout the world and are worth 10,000 each.
Collecting all of the coins and successfully rescuing the princess contributes to a special completion ending.

sections.title: Animated Environment
paragraphs: The sky and lava were animated using Perlin-noise-driven effects, adding continuous motion to the voxel environment.

sections.title: Artwork
paragraphs: I created the game's textures and environment presentation myself.
A collaborating artist in Sweden created the character artwork and still-image cutscene artwork.

sections.title: Completed Adventure
paragraphs: The final submission was not just a technical voxel demo. It was a complete playable adventure with an opening area, progression gates, interior regions, combat, collectibles, side content, a final boss-avoidance sequence, a rescue objective, and an ending.

sections.title: Performance Testing
paragraphs: I also used the completed level as a ShaderBox performance test and demonstrated approximately 50,000 animated red stick-figure characters running inside the world while maintaining smooth performance on 2013-era hardware.

sections.title: MolyJam Submission
paragraphs: The game was completed and uploaded to the MolyJam site before the submission deadline.
The site provided each participant with a dedicated project page for progress updates, final submission, and community ratings.

historicalNotes: The legacy portfolio card incorrectly spelled the event 'Molly Jam'; canonical spelling is 'MolyJam'.
This is the separate 2013 MolyJam project, not Escape from Mirror Mansion from MolyJam 2012.
The game was built during a 48-hour jam and submitted on time.
Jamie participated remotely from home through the worldwide MolyJam website.
Jamie was the sole developer.
The game was built directly on ShaderBox.
The level was hand-built in Qubicle rather than procedurally generated.
The voxel terrain was not destructible or editable during gameplay.
The game used a first-person perspective.
The player used a sword for combat.
There were approximately three troll enemy types.
The giant guarding the princess could not be killed; touching or being crushed by it killed the player.
The main progression path included the exterior world, the goblin-head mountain entrance, mountain interior, lava, temple, castle, summit, giant encounter, and princess rescue.
A pirate ship and river boat encounter provided additional exploration/gameplay.
The pursuing small boat fired a cannon at the player.
The tap opened the mouth of the giant goblin-head mountain.
The Peter Molydeux image-follow mechanic represented the 'most interesting thing in the world' prompt.
The golden acorn was obtained from a guarded/trapped temple.
Coins were worth 10,000 each.
Collecting all coins and rescuing the princess produced a special completion ending.
The sky and lava used animated Perlin noise.
Jamie created the game's textures.
A Swedish collaborating artist created character artwork and still-image cutscene artwork.
The artist's name is not currently recovered.
The complete gameplay video is available on YouTube and is stronger evidence of project scope than screenshots alone.
Jamie also demonstrated approximately 50,000 animated red stick figures inside the completed level as a ShaderBox performance test.
The exact hardware and measured frame rate for the 50,000-character test should not be claimed unless recovered from the original performance media.
This project is not the CaveGen game jam; CaveGen belongs to a separate upcoming card.
The original legacy wording 'Combined 5 themes' referred to combining five Molydeux quotes/prompts into one game.
